attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors measures how much one vector extends in the direction of another. Geometrically, it equals the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them. If the vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), their dot product is zero because cos(90°) = 0, meaning no projection onto each other. A negative dot product means the angle between vectors is greater than 90°, so one vector projects negatively onto the other, indicating they point more opposite than the same way.

attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors represents the product of their magnitudes and the cosine of the angle between them. Geometrically, it measures how much one vector projects onto another. When two vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), their dot product is zero because the cosine of 90° is zero, indicating no projection. A negative dot product means the angle between the vectors is greater than 90°, so the projection of one vector onto the other points in the opposite direction, reflecting a negative component along that vector.
